about: The version 2.1 acceptance portfolio (docs/audits/2026-09-27-v2.1-review/ACCEPTANCE.md). Twelve practical questions, each with the answer the source records support, written from data/tables and the cached, hash-checked sheets the records cite, before the code that meets them. Nothing here was copied from the engine's output. test/acceptance.test.js runs the engine on each and compares. An expectation marked todo names the work package that had not yet met it when it was written.
reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (an agent), 2026-09-28. No person has reviewed these answers yet; ACCEPTANCE.md lists what a reviewer should check.

cases.question: An outdoor bracket: heat deflection at 0.45 MPa at least 100 °C, XY stiffness at least 3 GPa, density at most 1500 kg/m³, printable on the H2C (nozzle, bed and chamber), used as printed.

expect.because: Polymaker FIBERON ASA CF08's own sheet: HDT 103 °C at 0.45 MPa, XY modulus 3.61 GPa, 1090 kg/m³; nozzle 260-280 °C, bed 90-100 °C, chamber room temperature. None of its values is stated as annealed.
The same values state neither the specimen form, the moisture state nor the post-processing: the screening policy admits them, and the verdict must say so.
3DXTECH FIBREX PA12 GF30 meets the three limits (V001014, V001009, V001007), but its print guide asks for a chamber up to 120 °C; the H2C reaches 65 °C.
Bambu Lab PPA-CF's sheet asks for a 50-80 °C chamber, which the H2C only partly reaches: unresolved, not failed.
Bambu Lab PA6-CF's sheet measures every property after annealing at 80 °C for 12 h; nothing says how the part performs as printed.
With annealing available, the annealed state meets every limit (HDT 186 °C, XY modulus 4.43 GPa) and the recipe is within the H2C: the verdict names the 80 °C, 12 h treatment.
A standard template asks whether the H2C can print the product (GOALS, 2026-09-28, decision 4).

cases.question: A warm polycarbonate component, through the Warm environment template: can the H2C print PC 275 and Kratos PC as their sheets ask?

expect.because: The bed is part of printing it; the template checked the nozzle and the chamber only.
Spectrum PC 275's sheet asks for a 90-130 °C bed; the H2C's reaches 120 °C.
FormFutura Kratos PC prints PC 275's sheet (the same Shared formulation key, D89), so its bed is PC 275's.

cases.question: A PET-GF fixture: XY stiffness at least 4 GPa and heat deflection at 0.45 MPa at least 80 °C, with and without an oven to anneal in.

expect.because: Fiberon PET-GF15 as printed: HDT 81.6 °C (V001931) meets the heat limit, but its only XY modulus, 4.14 GPa (V001934), is of bars annealed at 120 °C for 16 h. The two describe different states; the reason names the schedule that would settle it.
Annealed at 120 °C for 16 h (the schedule the sheet's recipe states, and the one its mechanical footnote names): XY modulus 4.14 GPa and HDT 133.7 °C, both of annealed bars.

cases.question: A PLA Matt part that must not soften below 100 °C (heat deflection at 0.45 MPa), with and without a permitted 90 °C, 4 h anneal.

expect.because: Spectrum PLA Matt's 116 °C is of a bar annealed for 4 h at 90 °C; the sheet gives no as-printed heat deflection.
With annealing available, the annealed state's 116 °C decides, and the verdict names the 90 °C, 4 h treatment.
The sheet prints 90 °C as the annealing temperature ('annealed (4h @ 90°C)'), not as a test temperature (re-read 2026-09-27).
The same line at 1.81 MN/m².

cases.question: A fixture in a humid room: XY stiffness at least 6 GPa after the part has taken up moisture.

expect.because: BASF Ultrafuse PAHT CF15 dry: XY modulus 8.39 GPa (V002469).
Conditioned, the same sheet prints 5.05 GPa (V002495). The dry value does not describe the humid service state.
Nanovia PA-6 CF publishes no conditioned value; nothing is inferred from its dry one.
PolyMax PETG-ESD's sheet rates weak acids Good and strong acids Fair-Poor (p. 2, re-read 2026-09-27). The Good cannot answer 'acids' while the strong-acid rating limits it.
3DXTECH 3DXSTAT ESD PETG has no acid record of its own; Q00107 is Polymaker's product's.

cases.question: ECOMAX PLA: does it resist water, and can it be bought in stock in Canada?

expect.because: 3DXTECH ECOMAX PLA has no water record of its own; the insolubility records are Bambu Lab's products'.
Bambu Lab PLA Basic's own sheet: insoluble in water.
No sampled Canadian offer is ECOMAX PLA's.
Bambu Lab Canada listed PLA Basic in stock.
PLA Basic Gradient's one sampled offer was out of stock; another product's stock is not its own.

cases.question: PLA for a part that must reach 3 GPa XY stiffness, in Include uncertain: several PLA products publish an XY modulus below it, and many publish none.

expect.because: No PLA product demonstrates 3 GPa, and those measured fail it; the unmeasured ones are unresolved, so the material is unresolved, not failed, and the counts say so.

cases.question: Warm environment, ranked by a light, stiff beam (E^1/2 / rho): does every view give the same order?

expect.because: One goal and one policy give one ranking: the table, the chart's guide and the export name the same materials in the same order, from passing products' own values.

cases.question: A part loaded across its layers, and one that must take a notched impact: XY never stands in for Z, and Charpy, Izod and J/m never stand in for each other.

expect.because: Its Z strength is 25 MPa (V006488); its XY 43.5 MPa (V006487) is another direction.
ECOMAX PLA publishes an XY strength only.
PC 275 publishes a notched Izod in J/m to ASTM D256, never a Charpy value.
An Izod value in J/m needs the bar's thickness to compare, which the sheet does not print (D94).

cases.question: A general prototype through the Indoor prototype template, where most products have no sampled price.

expect.because: Price sits late in the funnel (GOALS): a missing sample is a sourcing task, not a reason to hold a prototype material out.
ECOMAX PLA has no sampled offer; its answer must not rest on that.

cases.question: A decision saved against one release and reopened against another made the same day.

expect.because: Two releases with the same data date are different evidence; the reopened scenario says so.
The same release built again is the same evidence; no false alarm.
A scenario saved before releases were identified carries only a date; it says its identity cannot be checked.
A shared link carries the release it was made on.
